ticket: docs/wayfinder/tickets/07-acceptance-validator-spec.md; total-area quantity and convention agreement by docs/wayfinder/tickets/17-area-measurement-convention.md (ADR 0010); opening placement, the contact threshold and the party-face corrections by docs/wayfinder/tickets/16-opening-placement-rules.md (ADR 0021); ENGINE_CHOICE thresholds fitted, conf gains 'fitted', dim.max_area and dim.stated_target_implausible added, and dim.market_default_area made two-sided by docs/wayfinder/tickets/20-fit-engine-choice-thresholds-to-the-corpora.md (ADR 0023)
disclaimer: Neufert-grade dimensional standards (C8). Design data, not a building code. No legal code-compliance claim is made or implied by any rule in this file. Rules citing a regulatory document cite it as a source of dimensional fact, not as a compliance target.

units.note: All lengths integer millimetres, per ADR 0001. There are no tolerances in this file: junction closure, coincidence and zero-area are integer equalities, not epsilon comparisons. Tolerance exists only at import boundaries, which this file does not describe.

rule_format.description: Every rule is an object. The registry is the canonical statement of the Acceptance bar; the prose spec is a reading of it, not a second source.

keys.id: stable identifier, referenced by the solver, the validator and the Homeowner message catalogue
keys.item: which of C6's seven items this realises; 'extra' for the two the seven do not cover; 'model' for geometry-model integrity; 'programme' for a rule whose subject is the ResolvedBrief's multiset of Room types rather than any one entity
keys.statement: the predicate in one sentence, stated over the canonical geometry model's vocabulary
keys.value: the number, where the rule carries one
keys.src: key into the sources block of data/standards/room-constraints.json, or a corpus statistic where conf is fitted, or engine_choice, or pending
keys.conf: verified | reported | derived | fitted | engine_choice | pending
keys.note: required when conf is engine_choice, derived or pending, or when severity is deferred

severity_meanings.hard: a Plan failing this is not shown. Never.
severity_meanings.soft: scored; contributes to ranking among survivors; never rejects
severity_meanings.warn: surfaced to the Homeowner alongside a shown Plan; never rejects and never scores
severity_meanings.deferred: the rule is real and its source is recorded, but it cannot be evaluated in v1. Parked visibly rather than dropped silently.

site_meanings.solver: posted as a CP-SAT constraint over centreline grid coordinates, before any Opening exists
site_meanings.validator: evaluated on a finished Plan in clear integer millimetres over Spaces and Openings
site_meanings.both: posted and evaluated. Only these rules can be asserted to agree, and the conformance test asserts exactly this subset.

scope_meanings.plan: evaluated over a finished Plan's Spaces, Walls and Openings
scope_meanings.brief: evaluated over the ResolvedBrief, at parse time and again when no candidate survives
scope_meanings.note: A `programme` rule is brief-scope AND HAS NO PLAN-SIDE TWIN, which is deliberate. The Room set is frozen at `resolve`: brief.md §9.5 forbids auto-repair, §3 makes every Brief Room required, the warp maps a donor onto a fixed multiset, and model.no_unassigned_area forces every Room to become a Space. So a plan-side composition predicate could never fail on a Plan whose Brief passed -- and a rule that cannot fire is a lie about coverage, which is why win.habitable_touches_exterior was retired. ADR 0015 runs the other way, from a shipped Plan rule back to its parse-time pre-image; these four are the first rules with an image and no pre-image.

conf_meanings.verified: read directly from the primary document named in src
conf_meanings.reported: a credible third party attributes this value to src; not read first-hand
conf_meanings.derived: computed from a verified value by a stated rule
conf_meanings.fitted: no source dictates this; its value is a named statistic of a named corpus, and src says which. Weaker than a document, stronger than a judgement. ADR 0023. Every fitted rule also carries corpus_cost: the share of real dwellings the value rejects, measured in docs/research/acceptance-thresholds.md
conf_meanings.engine_choice: no source dictates this AND nothing has measured it; the engine picks it, and note says why. ADR 0023 narrowed this from unsourced to unmeasured
conf_meanings.pending: the value is owed and the rule ships without it

region_binding.comment: The hard rule set carries NO region. This is a v1 decision and it is load-bearing: the hard floor is the ergonomic minimum, which is body-derived and therefore region-invariant, so the predicates that reject a Plan are the same in every region. Region parameterises soft objectives only.
region_binding.consequence: Adding a region cannot change which Plans are rejected, only which are preferred. A region we have never surveyed still gets a defensible hard bar, which is what makes shipping without a settled region list possible.

tier_binding.comment: data/standards/room-constraints.json defines four tiers. The validator reads two. The other two stay in the schema, unread, so adopting them later is a configuration change rather than a rewrite.
tier_binding.supersedes: room-constraints.json tier_model.validator_binding, which named statutory_floor as the hard tier. That binding is unusable: statutory_floor is null for the default region because German law prescribes no minimum room areas, so it yields an empty hard set. See docs/spec/acceptance-bar.md section 3. Ticket 19 authored the layer and the key is `ergonomic`; both files now carry the same string, and the conformance test asserts it.
tier_binding.consequence: Ticket 07's hard-or-soft question is answered per-value by which tier the number came from. No rule carries a separate hard/soft flag for its dimensional numbers.

rules.statement: The Plan has exactly one Storey.
rules.note: C5. Inherited from Canonical geometry model, which made Storey explicit precisely so the bar could say this rather than leave it implied.

rules.statement: Every Wall centreline is axis-aligned: its endpoints share an x or share a y.
rules.note: v1 scope. Non-orthogonal geometry is fog on the map, not a relaxation of this rule.

rules.statement: Every Wall thickness is a member of the active region profile's thickness catalogue for its class.
rules.note: Standard thickness means catalogue membership, not a range. The UK values in the corpus are themselves ENGINE_CHOICE: findings section 5.6 records that no UK source prescribes them.

rules.statement: Every Wall centreline endpoint is integer-coincident with another Wall centreline or with the Envelope boundary. No endpoint is dangling.
rules.note: Integer equality, not tolerance. ADR 0001 deleted this question rather than answering it. A T-junction does not split the through wall; it records ATPATH.

rules.statement: For every pair of Spaces, the integer area of their rectangle intersection is zero.
rules.note: Derived from ADR 0001. Spaces are eroded rectangles in integer millimetres, so bounding-box overlap and true-polygon overlap are the same computation. The sibling project's bbox-versus-polygon comparison is discharged by construction; no C11 re-measurement is owed.

rules.statement: The union of all Space polygons and all Wall bodies equals the Envelope interior exactly.
rules.note: The validator form of the solver's soft-coverage amendment. Posted soft in the solver for search speed and checked hard here: identical semantics, and the place where a 29x-faster search is prevented from shipping a hole. The 24-room INVALID row in the solver findings, 141 cells unassigned, is exactly what this catches.

rules.statement: Every Space polygon equals its solved centreline rectangle eroded by t_int/2.
rules.note: The honesty check on a cheap derivation. Inherited verbatim from Canonical geometry model. It fails the day internal wall thickness stops being uniform, which is the point of keeping it.

rules.statement: Every Space area is at least the ergonomic minimum area for its Room type.
rules.note: UNBLOCKED by ticket 19. Values are per room type in the ergonomic layer, region-free, in m2 to one decimal, and each is short x long rounded DOWN so the rule cannot reject the rectangle it was derived from. Measured against Swiss Dwellings: the published floor rejects 0.0% of real living rooms and bedrooms, 1.2% of kitchens, 4.6% of WCs and 7.8% of storerooms. It binds independently of the two dimension rules because a room can clear both sides and still be long and thin; dim.aspect_ratio_hard catches that. PLANE NAMED by ticket 17 / ADR 0010: the Space polygon is now the FINISHED face, which is what the ergonomic minima always claimed to be and were not -- bathroom.min_clear_long is 1700 because a bath is 1700, and against a bare-masonry rectangle the bath did not fit. CAUTION carried rather than smoothed: the Swiss Dwellings validation quoted above measured corpus polygons whose own face convention is unrecorded. If those polygons are structural, the published floor is slightly LENIENT -- small, systematic, and in the wrong direction. Owed by *Look at the converted corpus*.
rules.ref: ergonomic layer, derived from fixture footprints + body zone

rules.statement: Every Space shorter clear dimension is at least min_clear_short for its Room type.
rules.note: UNBLOCKED by ticket 19. Clear, not centreline, per ADR 0001. The pair is (shorter side, longer side), NOT (x, y): a room has no canonical orientation, and stating the rule over the shorter and longer dimension is what lets a single pair describe a room that may sit either way round.

rules.statement: Every Space longer clear dimension is at least min_clear_long for its Room type.
rules.note: UNBLOCKED by ticket 19. This rule's previous note -- 'distinct from width only for bathroom and wc, whose fixture footprints are genuinely directional' -- is WITHDRAWN. The directional/orientation-free distinction findings section 8 drew does not survive the derivation: because the rule is stated over the shorter and longer dimension rather than over x and y, no room type needs an axis binding, and once fixtures actually drive the rectangle most types are non-square, not two. Only corridor is square, and only because it has no second dimension of its own.

rules.statement: Every Space of type corridor or hall has a clear width of at least 900 mm.
rules.note: Resolves C6 item 2's no-sub-1m-corridors placeholder. AD M's 750 mm relief for a localised obstruction over no more than 2 m, 2.22b, is DROPPED: a Space is a rectangle and has no localised anything, so the allowance could never fire. Corridors are pre-sized conservatively from the region profile's worst-case door arrangement, per Canonical geometry model, which is what keeps opening placement post-solve. CROSS-CHECKED by ticket 19: the ergonomic floor gives hall a min_clear_short of 900 as well, so this rule and the ergonomic floor agree on both types named here rather than one silently subsuming the other.

rules.statement: For every habitable or wet Space, the ratio of its longer to its shorter clear dimension is at most 3.0.
rules.note: No surveyed source states an aspect rule. Added because nothing in C6's seven items catches a room that meets its minimum area and its minimum width by being long: 2750 x 8250 is a compliant, unliveable bedroom, and it is the most likely way a passing Plan still reads as generated. corridor, hall and storage are exempt, being legitimately high-aspect.  || FITTED by *Fit the ENGINE_CHOICE acceptance thresholds to the corpora* (ADR 0023), docs/research/acceptance-thresholds.md. UNMOVED, and it is the p99.5 to two decimal places: over 235,045 binding rooms in 42,985 real Swiss dwellings, clear-plane bbox aspect has p95 2.14, p99 2.71, p99.5 3.02, max 6.85. Rejects 2.85 % of real dwellings -- the same tolerance *What a room's area is allowed to be* chose independently at p99.5 (3.1 %). ResPlan agrees and is looser (1.05 %), so Swiss is the corpus this is read off. The exemptions are vindicated too: corridor sits at p90 3.30, above the cap it is exempt from. WARNING for the proposer, not for this rule: on the CONVERTED corpus the same threshold costs 10.62 %, because the fit's second rectangle -- the leg of an L -- exceeds 3.0 at 19.55 % against 2.45 % for single-part Rooms. That is elongation the conversion manufactures, not elongation real rooms have.

rules.statement: Prefer habitable and wet Spaces with an aspect ratio at or below 2.2.
rules.note: Ranking term. Same exemptions as dim.aspect_ratio_hard.  || FITTED by *Fit the ENGINE_CHOICE acceptance thresholds to the corpora* (ADR 0023), docs/research/acceptance-thresholds.md. UNMOVED. 2.2 is the p95 (2.14) of the same distribution.

rules.statement: Prefer Spaces whose area is close to the target area for their Room type, penalised as soft_w[type] x |area - target_area|.
rules.note: The soft half of the C10 split, and region-dependent. A Plan built to the hard floor is valid and unliveable; this is the term that stops the solver settling there.  || MADE TWO-SIDED by *Fit the ENGINE_CHOICE acceptance thresholds to the corpora*, transcribing docs/research/room-area-bands.md 6.2 without re-deriving it. It was one-sided -- 'at or above market_default' -- so the objective actively REWARDED bloat while model.no_unassigned_area made the surplus compulsory. A maximum alone would have relocated the bloat to just under the cap. soft_w is measured, not chosen: it is 1/CV of each class's area dispersion, normalised, so a tight class resists growth and a loose one absorbs, and asking a Homeowner which room gets the leftover space is an architect's question put to someone C2 says cannot read a dimension string. Table at area_bands.classes.*.soft_w. conf stays engine_choice because the SHAPE of the penalty is a choice; its weights are fitted.

rules.statement: Every Space area is at most the upper band for its Room type: k[type] x Room.target_area where the Room has a target_area, and absolute_cap[type] where it has none.
rules.note: NEW. Every area predicate in this file was a floor or a total, so a 40 m2 WC passed the bar and model.no_unassigned_area made the surplus compulsory. Measured and reasoned in full at docs/research/room-area-bands.md 6.1; transcribed here by *Fit the ENGINE_CHOICE acceptance thresholds to the corpora*, which holds this file, and NOT re-derived. A STATED TARGET IS SOVEREIGN: the absolute cap is a fallback, not a ceiling, because C4 makes the Brief the real interface and the defect this rule fixes is an area the ENGINE invented. k is not one constant (2.02 to 8.15) and a single global k would be the invented number this rule exists to avoid. The solver side is FREE: H4 already builds a = w*h via AddMultiplicationEquality for the minimum, and an upper bound on a product tightens propagation on w and h rather than weakening it. The percentile is not free either: p95 rejects 26.6 % of real dwellings, p99 6.0 %, p99.5 3.1 % -- and this corpus is the retrieval and training population, so a rejection here is coverage lost. p99.5 is also the percentile at which the 4-room case stops being inexpressible. Reproduced independently by this ticket over 42,985 dwellings at 3.11 % against room-area-bands' 3.1 %. PROVENANCE: every number is Swiss and the profile is AZ. A maximum is NOT region-free the way dim.min_area is -- the ergonomic floor is region-free because a body is a body, and a maximum is a market fact with no such defence.

rules.statement: A stated Room target_area exceeds absolute_cap for its Room type.
rules.note: NEW, and it is the counterweight to dim.max_area's sovereignty of a stated target. Surfaced against the Brief exactly as area.given_envelope_warn is: it keeps the Homeowner sovereign while catching an LLM parse that put a decimal in the wrong place. Transcribed from docs/research/room-area-bands.md 6.3 by *Fit the ENGINE_CHOICE acceptance thresholds to the corpora*.

rules.statement: Over the contact graph, every Room receives flow from the entry Room, where a contact edge exists iff the shared wall run is at least the structural opening width plus t_int plus 400 mm.
rules.note: Solver-only by construction: it runs before any Opening exists. This is potential circulation, and it asserts only that a door COULD be placed. Formulation and contact threshold inherited from Solver formulation for layout projection and Canonical geometry model. AMENDED by Opening placement rules (ADR 0021 part 1): the threshold gains 400 mm. ADR 0001 consequence 3 is explicit that +t_int is only the centreline-to-clear correction, so the OLD threshold reserved exactly the structural opening and nothing else -- zero jamb, zero nib -- while open.fits_segment and open.leading_edge_nib hard-require 100 + w + 300 of CLEAR run on that same segment. A solve could pass this rule and be hard-rejected the moment a door was placed on the run it had just certified. The 400 is 100 jamb + 300 nib and is the same whichever end the door is pushed to. It also buys what docs/spec/openings.md 3.1 needs: under the old threshold a minimum-length contact admits exactly ONE door position, mid-wall, so the threshold was specifying the room an architect would redraw rather than merely permitting it. COST NOT MEASURED HERE: INFEASIBLE will rise; experiments/solver-toy/ belongs to What an ordered entry sequence costs the solver and the rate is handed there.

rules.statement: Over the opening graph, every Space is reachable from the entry Space, where an edge exists iff the WallSegment between the pair hosts at least one passable Opening.
rules.note: Validator-only by construction: Openings are placed after the solve. A window is never an edge. This is the rule that catches a valid solve handed no door, which potential circulation cannot see.

rules.statement: Every Space is reachable from the entry Space by at least one path traversing no Space whose Room has is_private true, except that a dependent Room is reached through its declared host.
rules.note: Solver form: private rooms may receive flow but never forward it. C6 item 1 as originally stated rejects every Plan with an ensuite, because an ensuite is reachable only through a bedroom and both are private. The dependent-room exception is what makes the rule survivable, and it makes it stronger: an ensuite reached from the hall now fails, which it should.

rules.statement: A Room declaring access_via has exactly one passable Opening, and it connects that Room to its declared host.
rules.note: access_via is a Brief field, not a geometric inference: access-through is program, not geometry. Propagates to Brief schema and parsing contract.

rules.statement: Prefer a total circulation Space area between 8 and 18 percent of the sum of Space areas.
rules.note: C6 item 7's sane fraction. NO surveyed source supplies one. Placeholder pending a fit against the corpora. Soft, so a wrong placeholder costs ranking quality and rejects nothing. DENOMINATOR NAMED by ticket 17 / ADR 0010: was 'GIA', which is not a quantity v1 computes. It is the sum of ALL Space areas, circulation included, which is az_umumi_sahe itself. The two differ by the partition footprint, roughly 4-5 percent. FREE TO CHANGE, because both numbers here are unfitted placeholders -- but the fit owed by *Fit the ENGINE_CHOICE acceptance thresholds to the corpora* must use THIS denominator, and must compute the corpus side the same way.  || FITTED by *Fit the ENGINE_CHOICE acceptance thresholds to the corpora* (ADR 0023), docs/research/acceptance-thresholds.md. MOVED, [0.08, 0.18] -> [0.09, 0.15]. Real circulation share over 42,985 dwellings: p25 0.092, p50 0.122, p75 0.151, p90 0.188. The old band held 71.31 % of real dwellings and held them asymmetrically (16.55 % below, 12.14 % above) against a p50 of 0.122. A soft band exists to RANK, and a band holding 71 % of the population is inert on 71 % of it, so it is fitted to the interquartile range. By construction a quarter of real dwellings sit each side. Also measured: 2.66 % of real dwellings have NO circulation Space at all, and resolve invents one unconditionally, so the engine cannot emit them.

rules.statement: Total circulation Space area does not exceed 30 percent of the sum of Space areas.
rules.note: An outer bound, not a quality bar. Set where it only ever catches Plans that are visibly broken, so it cannot become the 99-percent-rejection rule the ticket warns about. DENOMINATOR NAMED by ticket 17 / ADR 0010: was 'GIA', which is not a quantity v1 computes. It is the sum of ALL Space areas, circulation included, which is az_umumi_sahe itself. The two differ by the partition footprint, roughly 4-5 percent. FREE TO CHANGE, because both numbers here are unfitted placeholders -- but the fit owed by *Fit the ENGINE_CHOICE acceptance thresholds to the corpora* must use THIS denominator, and must compute the corpus side the same way.  || FITTED by *Fit the ENGINE_CHOICE acceptance thresholds to the corpora* (ADR 0023), docs/research/acceptance-thresholds.md. UNMOVED. p99 is 0.284 and p99.5 is 0.322, so 0.30 sits inside the tail exactly where this note already claimed, and rejects 0.69 % of real dwellings. The claim is now a measurement.

rules.statement: At least one Opening of kind entrance_door is hosted on a WallSegment of the pair {room, EXTERIOR} whose Envelope edge carries entrance_side.
rules.note: SHARPENED by Opening placement rules, from Building scope and envelope handling's handoff: the segment's edge must carry entrance_side. A flat's front door DOES pierce a party wall -- onto a common corridor -- which is why entrance_side is orthogonal to condition rather than a third value, and why this rule tests the flag and not the condition. docs/spec/openings.md 7 places the primary entrance on the invented hall's segment of such an edge.

rules.statement: Exactly one entrance_door carries is_primary true. It is the source node of the realised circulation graph.
rules.note: One by default, more allowed: a house may have a back door with is_primary false. A flat gets exactly one, because its Envelope is given and a second exterior door is a Brief error rather than a layout choice. Which Room holds the entrance, and where on its segment the door sits, are ASSUMPTIONS the engine defaults and surfaces rather than Brief requirements; the defaulting rule belongs to Opening placement rules.

rules.statement: Every Opening structural width plus twice the minimum jamb return does not exceed the CLEAR length of the WallSegment hosting it.
rules.note: The door-fits-its-wall half of C6 item 3, and also the rule that catches a window too wide for its exterior segment. value is the minimum jamb return per side. ENGINE_CHOICE: no surveyed source gives a minimum return. FACE DECLARED by Opening placement rules: CLEAR, not centreline. A WallSegment's length is a centreline length, so read literally this rule was 50 mm looser than it appears (t_int 150 against 2 x 100). Every dimension in this system declares clear or centreline and this one did not. Clear is the reading docs/spec/openings.md 3.2 assumes and the stricter of the two.  || FITTED by *Fit the ENGINE_CHOICE acceptance thresholds to the corpora* (ADR 0023), docs/research/acceptance-thresholds.md. UNMOVED. The fitted quantity is the HALF-SLACK, (clear run - structural width) / 2, because the predicate is a segment-LENGTH test. Over 693,976 real opening incidences the half-slack on doors sitting in an actual pier (run >= 1.5 m) has p1 114 mm and p5 383 mm, so 100 mm is below the p1 of what real construction leaves, and costs 0.92 % of those doors. Unfiltered the cost is 7.56 %, but 75.1 % of those failures sit on runs under 1.5 m where the opening IS the whole wall -- a cased or full-width opening, which has no jamb by construction. || ONE CONSTANT, TWO DOCUMENTS, AND BOTH READINGS HOLD. This rule tests the run's LENGTH and says nothing about where on the run the Opening sits -- the return itself is fixed by docs/spec/openings.md 3.2, at the same 100 mm at the pushed-to end. The split is deliberate: Openings are placed after the solve, so a placement is not a postable predicate. The corpus vindicates the placement constant too: real door jamb returns have p25 58 mm and p50 128 mm, so 100 mm sits at roughly the p40 and an engine door is never tighter to its corner than a median real one. 41.72 % of real doors sit tighter than the engine would place them and all of them pass this rule, correctly. What DOES cost something is the composite w + 400 that openings.md 3.2 needs whichever end the door is pushed to: 12.32 % of real doors sit on a run shorter than that, and that number belongs to open.leading_edge_nib and the solver reservation, not to this threshold.

rules.statement: Every hinged Opening swing footprint lies entirely within the Space it opens into.
rules.note: Swing footprint is the leaf-side square of side leaf_width anchored at the hinge: the bounding box of the swept quarter-disc. Conservative, integer, and evaluable with no fixture or furniture model, which v1 does not have.

rules.statement: No two swing footprints overlap.
rules.note: Generalises AD M's 1500 mm between lobby doors and between their swings. Expressed as footprint disjointness rather than as a distance, because disjointness is the property the distance was protecting, and it holds for every door arrangement rather than only for lobbies.

rules.statement: A 300 mm nib is clear at the leading edge of every door, maintained 1200 mm back into the receiving Space.
rules.ref: M4(2) 2.22; also BS 9266 for all rooms
rules.note: JUSTIFICATION RE-BASED by ADR 0021, constant unchanged. AD M's nib exists so a wheelchair user can reach the handle, and this profile has already refused an AD M accessibility figure -- body_zone is 300 and not AD M's 750. Keeping one while refusing the other needs a reason that is not preference: the 300 mm ALONG THE WALL is ergonomic before it is accessible -- architrave, handle, elbow -- and is what any architect leaves. The 1200 mm depth into the room is the accessibility half and costs no wall run, so it is kept unchanged rather than defended. The constant belongs to the region-invariant ergonomic layer, where the rest of the hard floor already lives.

rules.statement: An entrance-level WC door opens outwards, with the opening overlapping the pan by 250 mm.
rules.note: DEFERRED, not dropped. The predicate needs a pan, and fixtures are still fog on the map. Recorded with its source so that adopting it when fixtures land is a data change. A validator that silently omits a rule it cannot evaluate is indistinguishable from one that never knew about it.

rules.statement: Every Space whose Room has needs_window true hosts at least one window Opening on a WallSegment of that Space whose Envelope edge condition is exterior.
rules.note: TOPOLOGY, deliberately. The four regimes surveyed are not interconvertible: England imposes no daylight requirement at all, Germany measures the structural opening against net floor area, Japan's factor depends on distance to the site boundary and cannot be written as window_area >= k * floor_area, and the Metric Handbook needs reflectances a Plan does not carry. Topology is the part all four agree on. Physical fit is enforced by open.fits_segment. CORRECTED by Opening placement rules, from the handoff Building scope and envelope handling left here: a PARTY WALL IS External (CONTEXT.md, Wall), so 'External WallSegment' admitted a wall shared with a neighbour and a mid-block flat's bedroom could satisfy its daylight on it. The test is the Envelope edge's CONDITION, not the Wall's class. A party edge hosts no window; docs/spec/openings.md 6.1 places none there. This rule now also carries the kitchen, whose needs_window moves to true -- AzDTN 2.7-2 cl. 9.12 is verified and mandatory for living rooms AND kitchens. win.habitable_touches_exterior is NOT re-keyed: kitchen stays is_habitable false, because daylight and habitability are different questions AzDTN answers differently, and the facade contact arrives through this rule instead. Exposure cost handed to H8 and the single-aspect flat. || SITE MOVES TO `both`, AND THE PART IS DECLARED, by *H8 and the single-aspect flat*. This rule inherits the solver posting that win.habitable_touches_exterior carried before it was retired, and inherits it STRONGER: the solver posted mere contact, and what it posts now is the frontage budget itself -- each needs_window Room holds a run of EXTERIOR-condition Envelope edge of at least its catalogue window's structural width plus twice the jamb return (`value`, 100 mm per side, the same constant open.fits_segment uses). Without that posting the solver is blind to daylight and every candidate that misses it dies at validation, which is yield thrown away on a constraint the solver can already express: ADR 0003 types the edge ring before the solve. || PER ADR 0014 SS9.1 THIS BINDS PER ROOM -- a Room reaches its window through ANY of its parts -- BUT the WINDOW-BEARING PART must itself meet that Room's min_clear_short. That is the ticket's option 2, and it costs nothing today at one rectangle per Room while closing the alcove ADR 0014 opens: a habitable room whose only daylight comes down a 900 mm leg is an alcove with a window, not a room with an aspect. open.fits_segment already forces such a leg to 1400 mm for a bedroom window; the Room's own minimum is the number an architect would hold, and it is already published.  || FITTED by *Fit the ENGINE_CHOICE acceptance thresholds to the corpora* (ADR 0023), docs/research/acceptance-thresholds.md. The rule carries NO threshold to move -- it is topology -- so what is fitted here is its COST, reproduced independently of *H8 and the single-aspect flat*: 45.19 % of 42,985 real Swiss dwellings have at least one needs_window Room with no window incident on it, against H8's 43.3 %. It is the second-largest single contributor to the bar's rejection rate (15.97 points of the 84.41 % union) and it cannot be relaxed by moving a number. Measured with kitchen.needs_window TRUE, which is what room-constraints.json says again after this ticket repaired the silent revert recorded in docs/research/acceptance-thresholds.md section 10.

rules.statement: Prefer a total window structural-opening area of at least the region profile's fraction of the Space net floor area, where the windows counted are those on WallSegments whose Envelope edge condition is exterior.
rules.note: Re-sourced by ticket 25 off the dangling de_baybo key, which pointed at a deleted region. AzDTN 2.7-2 cl. 9.13 sets 1:8 as a LOWER bound for living rooms and kitchens, with NO upper cap -- read first-hand. The value is unchanged at 0.125, which two independent regulatory traditions now agree on. The 1:5.5 figure sometimes quoted alongside it is a MAXIMUM-glazing cap and belongs to SNiP 2.08.01-89*, repealed for AZ on 2021-11-30. The solver's soft objective target is the profile's 0.154, not this floor. Explicitly NOT hard: making it hard would encode one country's method as universal. 'Space net floor area' is the finished-face polygon, ADR 0010. || FACES DECLARED by *H8 and the single-aspect flat*, on the handoff *Opening placement rules* SS6.1 left: the run was computed over every boundary face, so a mid-block flat could satisfy its glazing ratio on a party wall. A party edge hosts no window (openings.md SS6.1), so only exterior-condition faces count. || SEVERITY HELD SOFT AND CHALLENGED. AzDTN 2.7-2 cl. 9.13 is `verified` and mandatory, which makes this the only statutory minimum on the map posted soft. It is held soft here because C14 names it -- 'one soft window fraction' -- and a window ticket is the wrong door to amend a standing constraint through. Ticketed as *A statutory floor, posted soft, in the one region v1 ships*.

rules.statement: The wet Spaces form at most two plumbing groups, where a group is a maximal set connected by shared WallSegments.
rules.note: Resolves a real disagreement between the two consumers. Solver formulation posts wet clustering as hard flow over the wet subset, which demands ONE group and so rejects a kitchen at the front with a bathroom at the back: a real home, not a defect. Scoring it purely soft lets a candidate through with five isolated stacks. A bound on the group COUNT stays postable as a hard constraint and matches the shape real dwellings take.  || FITTED by *Fit the ENGINE_CHOICE acceptance thresholds to the corpora* (ADR 0023), docs/research/acceptance-thresholds.md. MOVED, 2 -> 3, and the ticket predicted it in advance: *if the tail reaches 3, the hard bound is wrong.* Over 42,985 real dwellings the wet-group count is 1 at 39.05 %, 2 at 46.49 %, THREE AT 14.14 % and 4 at 0.20 %. So 'two is the shape real dwellings take' is true of the MODE and false of the tail, and the bound at 2 rejected one real home in seven. At 3 it costs 0.20 % and still refuses the five-isolated-stacks candidate that scoring this purely soft would admit. The measurement is conservative in the safe direction: contact at tau 0.30 m merges corner-touching groups, so the true count is at least what was measured. CONSEQUENCE: wet.shared_wall_length is now the only wet-adjacency rule with a gradient, and it scores zero on the 39.05 % whose wet rooms connect through a corridor rather than a wall.

rules.statement: Prefer greater total shared WallSegment length between wet Spaces.
rules.note: The quality gradient inside the hard bound of wet.plumbing_group_count.

rules.statement: The Brief target_area carries an area_convention.
rules.note: A BRIEF error, not a Plan error: it rejects the request, not the candidates. An area value without its convention is meaningless and differs by tens of percent for the same building. Ticket 17 re-sourced the example off the deleted DE/UK framing: the live case is a Baku listing quoting az_umumi_sahe INCLUDING an eyvan at coefficient 1.0 -- full area -- against a v1 target_area that excludes it. Propagates to Brief schema and parsing contract.

rules.statement: The Brief target_area_convention equals the area_convention of the Plan's region profile.
rules.note: ADDED by ticket 17 / ADR 0010, and it is the rule the ticket existed to produce. area.convention_declared only checks that a convention is PRESENT; presence without agreement is exactly the silent failure -- two numbers compared that are not the same quantity, with nothing raising a hand. A BRIEF error: v1 does not convert between conventions, because the deductions that separate them are unrepresentable here, so a mismatch has no honest resolution but to ask. With one shipping profile this can only fire when a Homeowner names a foreign convention, which is rare and is precisely when a silent pass would be worst.

rules.statement: Where the Envelope is invented, the sum of Space areas is within 5 percent of the Brief target_area, both stated in the same area_convention.
rules.note: Applies to houses. The engine chose the footprint, so drift is the engine's fault and is rejectable. QUANTITY CHANGED by ticket 17 / ADR 0010: was 'Plan GIA'. az_umumi_sahe sums room areas and does NOT count internal partitions; GIA does. On a 90 m2 dwelling that difference is 5.7 percent of Sum(Space area) at the shipped t_int of 150 -- WIDER than this gate, measured over 14,063 dwellings by ticket 33. The 4-5 percent first written here is verified for the corpus (4.8) and for the 120 mm ADR 0010 replaced (4.5), and was stale for 150. Under the old quantity the rule was near-vacuous, because an engine that sets the Envelope inner area to target passes by construction. Under this one it must control the partition footprint too, which is only known after the solve. The 5 percent is unchanged and remains UNFITTED -- it was never measured against the old quantity either, and it is now a harder gate. Re-fit when a real Proposer has run.  || FITTED by *Fit the ENGINE_CHOICE acceptance thresholds to the corpora* (ADR 0023), docs/research/acceptance-thresholds.md. UNMOVED, and decided against the 250 mm grid rather than against a solver spread, because no solver GIA spread exists on this map and the grid dominates anyway: model.no_unassigned_area is HARD, so Sum(Space) + wall bodies = the Envelope interior exactly and the solver has no packing freedom left to drift with. Re-expressing every real room with both dimensions rounded to 250 mm moves Sum(Space area) by p50 0.90 %, p95 2.64 %, p99 3.57 %. The grid alone crosses 5 % in 0.10 % of dwellings, so 5 % is 1.9x the p95 of the residual with room left for the solve.

rules.statement: Where the Envelope is invented, prefer a sum of Space areas within 2 percent of target_area.
rules.note: Quantity changed with area.invented_envelope_hard. Ticket 17 / ADR 0010.  || FITTED by *Fit the ENGINE_CHOICE acceptance thresholds to the corpora* (ADR 0023), docs/research/acceptance-thresholds.md. MOVED, 2 % -> 3 %. The 250 mm grid alone misses a 2 % target in 13.71 % of real dwellings. A soft preference the engine cannot meet for reasons unconnected to design is a constant term in the objective rather than a gradient. 3 % costs 2.85 %.

rules.statement: Where the Envelope is given, warn when the sum of Space areas differs from the Brief target_area, and surface it against the Brief.
rules.note: Applies to flats. Total area is fixed by the given Envelope, so EVERY candidate drifts by the same amount, and rejecting on it would reject 100 percent of them for a fault none of them caused. The ticket names a rule that rejects 99 percent as a bug in the rule; this is the 100 percent case, and it is a Brief inconsistency the layout cannot fix. QUANTITY CHANGED by ticket 17 / ADR 0010, and the change BITES HERE: the sum of Space areas is NOT fixed by the Envelope -- it falls as the layout adds partitions -- so unlike GIA this quantity does vary between candidates of one Envelope. It stays a warn, because the variation is small against the Brief-versus-Envelope gap that dominates it, but the stated reason is now only mostly true and is recorded as such rather than smoothed.

rules.statement: The ResolvedBrief contains at least one Room whose type is kitchen, kitchen_dining or living_dining_kitchen.
rules.note: AzDTN cl. 5.2 <<metbex (ve ya taxca-metbex)>>, register `nezerde tutulmalidir` = mecburi. REJECTS 5.99% OF REAL DWELLINGS. `taxca-metbex` has no Brief type -- room-constraints.json areas_m2.kitchen_niche.reachable_in_v1 records that narrowing -- and a niche is expressed as a `kitchen`, so this limb is satisfied by the niche case rather than blind to it. Corpus cost measured over 46,800 real Swiss dwellings with fixtures as ground truth -- Swiss Dwellings carries TOILET, BATHTUB, SHOWER, KITCHEN and BUILT_IN_FURNITURE features, so composition is observed and not inferred from room labels. Harness and figures on ticket 42. CH provenance against an AZ rule is C14's normal case.

rules.statement: The ResolvedBrief contains at least one Room whose type is bathroom, shower_room or bathroom_combined.
rules.note: AzDTN cl. 5.2 <<vanna otagi (ve ya dus)>>, the FIRST of the clause's two sanitary axes. REJECTS 7.33% OF REAL DWELLINGS. bathroom_combined satisfies this limb and prog.wc_exists out of one room, which is what a combined unit is. Corpus cost measured over 46,800 real Swiss dwellings with fixtures as ground truth -- Swiss Dwellings carries TOILET, BATHTUB, SHOWER, KITCHEN and BUILT_IN_FURNITURE features, so composition is observed and not inferred from room labels. Harness and figures on ticket 42. CH provenance against an AZ rule is C14's normal case.

rules.statement: The ResolvedBrief contains at least one Room whose type is wc, shower_room or bathroom_combined.
rules.note: AzDTN cl. 5.2 <<tualet (ve ya birlesdirilmis sanitar qovsagi)>>, the SECOND axis, and the rule this ticket exists for: before it, a Brief naming a living room, a bedroom, a kitchen and a bathroom passed all 36 predicates and exported a valid IFC of a flat with no toilet. THE SATISFYING SET IS THE DECISION, AND IT COST A ROOM TYPE. `bathroom` is NOT in it: its ergonomic rectangle is bath plus body zone and holds no pan, and the note that once claimed a pan and basin was arithmetically impossible -- bath 1.19 + pan 0.35 + basin 0.27 = 1.81 m2 of fixture in a 1.70 m2 room -- so it is struck. `shower_room` IS in it, because its programme composes the tray AND the pan. `bathroom_combined` is a NINETEENTH ROOM TYPE, added by this rule because without it the rule is unshippable: over the eighteen it rejected 48.32% of real dwellings, and 43.13 of those points were dwellings that HAVE a toilet -- in a room with a bath -- that the vocabulary could not say had one. With the type the cost falls to 5.19%, which is dwellings with no toilet anywhere: the defect, not the vocabulary. Corpus cost measured over 46,800 real Swiss dwellings with fixtures as ground truth -- Swiss Dwellings carries TOILET, BATHTUB, SHOWER, KITCHEN and BUILT_IN_FURNITURE features, so composition is observed and not inferred from room labels. Harness and figures on ticket 42. CH provenance against an AZ rule is C14's normal case.

rules.statement: The ResolvedBrief contains at least one Room whose type is storage.
rules.note: AzDTN cl. 5.2 <<yignaq otagi (ve ya divar teserrufat skafi)>>, mandatory in the same register as the other three -- AND IT SHIPS SOFT, WHICH IS A DEPARTURE STATED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED. Hard, it rejects 73.35% of real dwellings, against the 43.3% this map already calls large on win.habitable_has_window, and it carries no threshold to move. Two facts stop that number being evidence the room does not matter, and they point opposite ways. The norm's own alternative `divar teserrufat skafi` is a BUILT-IN WARDROBE -- furniture v1 does not model -- so the limb is partly unsatisfiable rather than merely expensive: crediting BUILT_IN_FURNITURE features still only reaches 30.19%. And a Swiss flat's storage is typically a Keller OUTSIDE the dwelling, which a dwelling-scoped corpus cannot see, so 73.35% overstates the case against the room. A warn is reachable -- the Homeowner resolves it by naming a `storage` -- where a hard rule would refuse three real dwellings in four. Corpus cost measured over 46,800 real Swiss dwellings with fixtures as ground truth -- Swiss Dwellings carries TOILET, BATHTUB, SHOWER, KITCHEN and BUILT_IN_FURNITURE features, so composition is observed and not inferred from room labels. Harness and figures on ticket 42. CH provenance against an AZ rule is C14's normal case.

homeowner_surface.principle: A predicate id is never shown. Every rule maps to a plain-language message and, where one exists, the Brief field whose edit would resolve it.

no_survivors.behaviour: diagnose; never show a failing Plan
no_survivors.rationale: CONTEXT.md states that a Plan failing the bar is not shown, and that invariant is the whole point of the bar. A Homeowner cannot judge a plan annotated with three defects, and relaxing the hard set to fill a gallery would make the bar advisory.
no_survivors.diagnosis_source: the ergonomic minima, arithmetically: the sum of hard minimum areas for the Brief's rooms plus a circulation allowance is a lower bound on a feasible GIA, computable without search
no_survivors.example: Three bedrooms, a bathroom and a kitchen need at least 58 m2. Your brief says 45 m2.
no_survivors.also: report the dominant hard failure across the rejected batch, in Homeowner language, leading with the Brief field to edit

conformance.comment: The written-once-consumed-twice guarantee is bought here, not by shared code. The solver posts inequalities over centreline grid coordinates before geometry exists; the validator evaluates finished geometry in clear millimetres; rules about Openings are unpostable because Openings are placed after the solve. Two implementations are structural, so agreement is tested rather than assumed.
conformance.test: for a generated population of Plans spanning feasible and infeasible Briefs, the solver's satisfaction of each site=both rule and the validator's evaluation of it agree on every Plan
conformance.subset_size_note: MOVED 14 -> 15 by *Fit the ENGINE_CHOICE acceptance thresholds to the corpora*, which added dim.max_area at site both. That is intended, not incidental: docs/research/room-area-bands.md 6.1 specifies the rule as hard at both and shows the solver side is FREE -- H4 already builds a = w*h via AddMultiplicationEquality for the minimum, and an upper bound on a product tightens propagation rather than weakening it. *A dwelling with no toilet passes every check* said the subset 'stays at 14 and cannot grow here', which was a constraint on THAT ticket (its programme rules are scope brief and have no plan-side twin), not a bar on the subset ever growing. The count is stated in prose in docs/spec/acceptance-bar.md and is now stale there.

retired.was: Every Space whose Room has is_habitable true shares at least one WallSegment with the EXTERIOR.
retired.why: RETIRED by *H8 and the single-aspect flat* (2026-08-26). It could not fire. Every room type with is_habitable true also carries needs_window true -- the 18-row table has no exception -- and win.habitable_has_window requires the window to sit on a segment whose Envelope edge condition is EXTERIOR. Hosting a window on an exterior segment implies sharing one, so this predicate was strictly implied by a rule already hard. Measured on 561 real Swiss dwellings it fails 11.9 percent against has_window's 43.3 percent, and every dwelling it rejects is a subset of the ones has_window rejects. The invariant it appeared to protect -- is_habitable implies needs_window -- was never carried by this rule; it is asserted directly by experiments/region-profile/ergonomic_check.py, which is where it belongs, because it is a property of the TABLE, not of a Plan. A rule that cannot fire is a lie about coverage: the conformance test can never exercise it.

retired.was: Warn when a kitchen Space has no window.
retired.why: RETIRED, on the handoff *Opening placement rules* left for whichever ticket next held docs/spec/acceptance-bar.md. Since ergonomic.rooms.kitchen.needs_window became true, win.habitable_has_window carries the kitchen HARD and this warn is unreachable. It was kept only because retiring it moves the rule count and that file was claimed elsewhere; this ticket holds it, so the count moves here. Its AzDTN cl. 9.12 sourcing is not lost -- it lives on profiles.AZ.windows.kitchen_windowless and in win.habitable_has_window's own note.

programme_rules.source: AzDTN 2.7-2 cl. 5.2, register `nezerde tutulmalidir` = mecburi (mandatory). Verified, first-hand, in experiments/finish-layer/out/azdtn_2_7_2.txt.
programme_rules.clause: <<Menzillerde yasayis otaqlari ve yardimci saheler: metbex (ve ya taxca-metbex), holl, vanna otagi (ve ya dus) ve tualet (ve ya birlesdirilmis sanitar qovsagi), yignaq otagi (ve ya divar teserrufat skafi) nezerde tutulmalidir.>>
programme_rules.why_five_limbs_are_not_one_rule: The clause has five limbs and they do not carry one severity. Written as a single predicate it would take the severity of its weakest limb -- storage, which rejects 73.35% of real dwellings -- and the WC would inherit it. One rule per limb is what lets three be hard and one warn, each with its own corpus cost on the record.
programme_rules.holl_is_asserted_not_tested: The `holl` limb has NO RULE, on purpose. brief.md §3.1: if the ResolvedBrief contains no `hall`, resolve invents one, so every ResolvedBrief has exactly one and the predicate is true by construction. Writing it anyway would add a rule that can never fire, which is what retired win.habitable_touches_exterior. Recorded here so the clause's coverage stays legible: five limbs, four rules, one invariant.
programme_rules.c8_and_c14: These are the FIRST hard rules on this map sourced to a region document, and neither C8 nor C14 is bent to allow it. C14 says a REGION PROFILE never changes which Plans are rejected -- these rules are not in a profile. They sit in the region-invariant rule set and are keyed on region-invariant Room TYPES. What AzDTN supplies is the FACT that a dwelling owes a kitchen, a washing room and a WC, and 94.01% / 92.67% / 94.81% of real SWISS dwellings agree with it -- which is the test that the fact is about homes and not about Azerbaijan. C8 is honoured in the other direction too: cl. 5.10 confines the combined sanitary unit to one-otaq state and municipal social stock, and this file DOES NOT ENFORCE THAT, because it is a compliance target rather than a dimensional or programmatic fact -- and 67.24% of real dwellings combine, so it does not describe practice either.
programme_rules.no_auto_repair: resolve does NOT invent a missing wc, kitchen or storage, and the asymmetry with the invented hall is deliberate. brief.md §9.5 forbids auto-repair; the hall is exempt because ADR 0013 requires the engine room count fixed before any geometry exists and no Homeowner ever states circulation. A Homeowner who omits a toilet has made a statement about the home, and inventing one silently spends a room out of C13's 3-10 gate -- a Brief at ten rooms would be refused BECAUSE WE ADDED ONE. The refusal names the field instead, per brief.md §9.4 bound 8.
programme_rules.message_locale: All four messages are Azerbaijani per homeowner-surface.md §2, so these rules arrive already owing the locale dimension the other 36 owe. They do not make that schema change; they enlarge it from 36 rules to 40.

area_bands.comment: The upper half of the dimensional band, measured in docs/research/room-area-bands.md and transcribed here by *Fit the ENGINE_CHOICE acceptance thresholds to the corpora*. target is the corpus p50, absolute_cap the p99.5, k the ratio the rule multiplies a STATED target by, and soft_w the normalised 1/CV that says which class absorbs slack.
area_bands.provenance_warning: Every number here is Swiss and the shipping profile is AZ. Third documented instance of C14's RegionProfile / CorpusProvenance mismatch, and the second that is a number rather than a layout.
area_bands.k_is_not_one_constant: 2.02 to 8.15, and the spread is not noise. The habitable rooms AZ actually sizes cluster at 2.0-2.6; the outliers are exactly the four types AZ ships as market_default None, plus dining and storeroom.
area_bands.owed: brief.md 9.4's f_hi/f_lo per-n table is a parse-time constant of the same kind and belongs beside this block rather than inline in prose. *The partition footprint has a mean and no spread* raised it; not taken here because it is brief.md's findings schema and moving it without its consumer would strand it.

envelope_constants.comment: Handed to this file by *Building scope and envelope handling* via *Fit the ENGINE_CHOICE acceptance thresholds to the corpora*. These are NOT acceptance rules -- they are the constants brief.md section 5 rung 2 uses to INVENT an Envelope when the Homeowner states neither dimensions nor a total area. They live here because this is the file that holds fitted numbers and brief.md section 12 named this ticket as their owner.

efficiency.note: interior = Sum(Room.target_area) / efficiency. Fitted as Sum(named-room area) / interior over 42,985 dwellings -- NAMED, because no Brief names a corridor (C13) and the factor exists to absorb the circulation the engine invents plus the internal wall footprint. p5 0.750, p25 0.813, p50 0.8423, p75 0.872, p95 0.923. Shipped at ~0.85, which was 0.9 % high. NOT used on brief.md 5 rung 1, where a stated target_area is scaled by the measured partition footprint f instead.

default_aspect.note: longer / shorter of the minimum rotated rectangle of the dwelling interior. p25 1.172, p50 1.376, p75 1.702, p95 2.362. Shipped at ~1.35, which was 1.9 % low.

exposure_mix.note: DISCHARGED ELSEWHERE, recorded here so nobody measures it twice. *The exposure presets were fitted to a measurement of one room* measured the ring-shape vector: four-sided 63.3 %, three-sided 26.0 %, adjacent pair 4.6 %, opposite pair 3.8 %, single 2.2 %. The three flat presets name 10.6 % of the corpus between them.

partition_footprint_cross_check.note: NOT a replacement for brief.md 5 rung 1's f = 0.0575. This is the partition footprint measured GEOMETRICALLY from the corpus's own wall gaps (p50 4.00 % of interior, 4.17 % of Sum(Space area)); f is computed at the SHIPPED t_int of 150. The corpus's own p50 wall gap is 99 mm, and 99/150 = 0.66 against 4.17/5.75 = 0.725, so the two agree once the plane is named. f = 0.0575 is the right number for a plan built at 150 mm, which is what rung 1 sizes. Recorded as an independent check of *The partition footprint has a mean and no spread* from a different direction.

rule_count_note: 36 -> 40 by *A dwelling with no toilet passes every check* (four programme rules), 40 -> 42 by *Fit the ENGINE_CHOICE acceptance thresholds to the corpora* (dim.max_area, dim.stated_target_implausible). Two retired rules sit outside this count in `retired`. This field exists because the count was previously stated only in prose, in four places in acceptance-bar.md and once in brief.md, and every ticket that moved it had to move them all.

owed.comment: What this file still owes, written HERE rather than only on the map. *The partition footprint has a mean and no spread* exists because two numbers were handed to a file nobody held; a list that lives in the file cannot be lost that way. Added by *Fit the ENGINE_CHOICE acceptance thresholds to the corpora*.

items.what: five zoning rules, specified ready to transcribe
items.detail: docs/research/zoning.md section 5b. One hard -- zone.sleeping_group_count, at most two sleeping groups, 97.5 % of real dwellings -- and four soft or warn, of which zone.no_social_transit is the one nobody had written: circ.no_private_transit blocks routing through a bedroom and NOTHING blocks routing through the living room, which 18.2 % of real dwellings do. Needs data/standards/room-constraints.json's is_sleeping flag, which *Where a set-versus-set property lives* also handed over and which may NOT be folded into is_private (true on the wet types too).
items.why_not_here: A threshold fit and a zoning vocabulary are different decisions, and transcribing five rules would move the rule count a third time while acceptance-bar.md is already six statements behind this file.

items.detail: ADR 0014 binds minima and aspect per part and area per Room, and a solver left to choose takes a second rectangle on a fifth to a third of the Rooms it is offered against a truth needing none. This is the term that prefers one. It is also what stands between the engine and the elongation the conversion manufactures -- 19.55 % of two-part legs exceed dim.aspect_ratio_hard against 2.45 % of single-part Rooms (docs/research/acceptance-thresholds.md 2.3).

items.what: a locale dimension on every Homeowner-facing message
items.detail: Section 11 requires a plain-language message per rule; all 42 are English and the surface is Azerbaijani. A SCHEMA change, not a translation pass -- and it is ONE schema change with brief.md 9.4, which returns a set of findings each carrying a severity, a Brief field and an Azerbaijani message.

items.what: brief.md 9.4's f_hi/f_lo per-n table belongs in data
items.detail: An eight-row parse-time constant of the same kind as area_bands, currently inline prose. It moves with 9.4's findings schema, not before it.

items.what: wet.shared_wall_length has no gradient on two dwellings in five
items.detail: With wet.plumbing_group_count at 3 (ADR 0023) this soft term is the only thing preferring two wet zones over three, and 39.05 % of real dwellings have wet rooms that connect through a corridor rather than a wall, so it scores zero on them. Distribution at docs/research/acceptance-thresholds.md 5.

stale_elsewhere: docs/spec/acceptance-bar.md states the rule count in four places and the site=both conformance subset once. Both moved: 40 -> 42 and 14 -> 15.
Six rule statements were amended by *Opening placement rules* and diverge from the prose that publishes them; this ticket amended nine more and added two.

docs/spec/acceptance-bar.md section 6's table and section 9.1 both state open.fits_segment as a jamb-return rule. It is a segment-LENGTH rule and binds no return -- docs/research/acceptance-thresholds.md 6.3.

corpus_cost_note: Every conf: fitted rule carries corpus_cost -- the share of real Swiss dwellings that rule alone rejects, over 42,985 in-band dwellings. The conjunction is NOT their sum and is worth knowing: the hard registry rejects 84.41 % as shipped and 82.31 % under the values in this file, with eleven of thirteen hard rules costing under a third of a point between them. Two rules carry all of it -- open.fits_segment and win.habitable_has_window -- and neither has a threshold that could be loosened to move it. Read open.fits_segment on real piers rather than on full-width openings and the union is 61.23 %. docs/research/acceptance-thresholds.md section 11.
